scope: Observed agreement on the frozen captured-race dataset. Pre-finish movement uses the existing replay cadence and wire precision. Skill starts use the existing 0.1 ms comparison. These captures informed the fixes; this is not an independent or population-wide accuracy estimate.

fixes.rule: Apply an already queued bonus on the final ordered detail update before retiring the detail. Original receivers still expire and new triggers after expiry are rejected.

Store normalized distance times 0.6f as float32; calculate complement and lane scale together in wider precision, then store the float32 limit. Apply the same inclusive boundary in lane and field queries.
fixes.evidence: The rounding order is inferred from captured boundary outcomes and checked across the corpus; it is not a claim of direct server-code verification.

fixes.rule: Round gap / 62.5 to float32 before adding the 0.8 minimum and capping at 1.6.

auditProjections: Recorded durations truncate the wider product of stored float32 duration and 10000; startup events use -1.
Official visual recipient masks describe the first ability, not the union of every gameplay ability recipient.

postFinish.scope: Post-finish official samples for every runner whose frames changed in the audited packets. Uses the existing wire quantization and additionally checks rushing and front-blocker identity. Unchanged races are not newly audited after finish.

verification.method: Each race was resimulated from its hash-verified pre-race input. Byte-identical full packets inherit the earlier complete score; changed packets are rescored. The optimized build is independently rerun and every complete packet must match the scored build.
verification.initialHarnessFailure: The first long-lived Python worker pool terminated with an access violation in the comparison harness after more than 9000 records. Its incomplete output was not used as the completed audit; bounded worker lifetimes were used for the successful audit.
